notes.body: @pquantin, Please review this split PR from https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/3740. Thanks very much.

added 1308 commits
  • 03a524e1...7028646f - 1307 commits from branch wireshark:master
  • de8e6ebb - MBIM: dissect low level UICC access commands
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/5188/diffs?diff_id=284645251&start_sha=03a524e11c4fcce722f2117bcccef7513600905c)
hf_mbim_ms_open_channel_app_id is defined as FT_UIN32 so this seems suspicious. Should if be FT_BYTES instead?
Note that Wireshaerk includes a STK dissector that you should be able to call for several of those UICC commands. See the mbim_dissect_set_stk_terminal_response() function.

Could you please share more details like which command DataBuffer can leverage dissect_cat since I checked the function dissect_cat a little bit and not sure which command DataBuffer can be dissected further by dissect_cat?
For example Open Channel and Close Channel are STK commands that can be dissected by dissect_cat(), as seen in packet-etsi_card_app_toolkit.c

Here is the Open Channel MBIM structure
![image](/uploads/07e1681bab00cd175e891f288f69ccab/image.png)

I think it is different and cannot be directly dissected by dissect_cat
But what is inside the AppId DataBuffer? Presumably this is the STK command sent to the UICC? Anyway this is not that important, but be aware that further dissection might be achievable.

Thanks very much for your review. Right, its DataBuffer may be able to be dissected further. But MBIM document doesn't provide enough information. I will remember this, if I have further information that its DataBuffer format can be dissected by dissect_cat, I will update it.
